episode_title: Key Considerations for Acquiring A Business

real_qa.q: What are the main differences between asset purchase and stock purchase in a business acquisition?
real_qa.r: Asset purchases offer tax benefits, liability protection, and the option to select which assets to acquire, with accelerated depreciation possibilities. Stock purchases mean taking on existing debt, inheriting all contracts and liabilities, and exposing yourself to hidden risks and unresolved obligations from the seller.
real_qa.requete: asset purchase vs stock purchase acquisition

real_qa.q: What critical due diligence steps must be completed before signing a Letter of Intent in a business acquisition?
real_qa.r: You must review P&Ls and tax returns, analyze accounts receivable, understand employee compensation and contracts, review customer contracts and data privacy, verify licenses and certifications, check OSHA compliance, and identify all lease agreements with amendments before signing an LOI. You cannot begin due diligence after signing—it must be done ahead of time.
real_qa.requete: business acquisition due diligence checklist LOI

real_qa.q: Why are lease agreements often deal-killers in business acquisitions?
real_qa.r: Landlords have killed more deals than can be named. You must know every lease, every amendment whether there is one or twenty, renewal options, and whether the lease will cash flow. Increasingly, landlords now negotiate to receive a piece of the sale price as part of the transaction, which must be factored into the deal structure.
real_qa.requete: lease agreements business acquisition deal killed

real_qa.q: What are the main regulatory compliance risks to assess when acquiring a business?
real_qa.r: You must verify licensing, data privacy protections, workplace safety (OSHA), EEOC compliance, HIPAA for healthcare, and industry-specific regulations like those for construction or electrical businesses. One misstep on compliance can result in inherited liabilities, fines, and operational shutdowns post-acquisition.
real_qa.requete: regulatory compliance business acquisition OSHA EEOC HIPAA

real_qa.q: What percentage of customer base may leave after combining two businesses operationally?
real_qa.r: Statistically, 10% to 25% of the customer base may leave when two businesses are combined, particularly when merging banking systems or operational platforms. This attrition must be built into financial projections and transition planning.
real_qa.requete: customer attrition rate business acquisition integration

real_qa.q: Why is selecting the right tax advisor critical in a business acquisition deal?
real_qa.r: Not all CPAs are created equal; some can calculate tax depreciation, goodwill allocations, sales tax, and non-compete allocations, while others simply prepare tax returns. The buyer and seller must file matching information with the IRS post-acquisition, and mismatches trigger audits. The wrong advisor makes the deal extremely difficult or a deal-killer.
real_qa.requete: tax advisor business acquisition CPA depreciation
